gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-runic: Noto Sans Runic is a plain sans with a big x-height and curves that never curl shut. College, up top, draws every curve as heavy as its stems, so shrinking it to small sizes would clog those wide counters.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-saurasht: Quiet and low-slung, Noto Sans Saurashtra keeps its capitals barely above the lowercase and its counters open to the outside. College never wavers in stroke weight, and the body font keeps a long page moving without any fuss.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sc: Chalky curves that stop short of closing give Noto SC its look. College holds one constant stroke with no pinched joins, and Noto Sans SC keeps a long passage moving smoothly, its low ascenders never tripping the eye.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Authoritative describes College, whose arches match the stems beside them in thickness. But Noto Sans Sharada, with its open c forms and bulky lowercase, is what carries the reading, while the heading does its best work big and loud.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Approachable is the first word for Noto Sans Siddham, with its large central band and an s whose ends hang far from the spine. And College sits above it with a stroke that never shifts from heavy to light, so the two read as one tidy page.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its curve endings keeping well apart from each other. College is best at shouting in a monoline pen stroke, while the body quietly does the reading.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: College draws a skeleton outline in one fixed stroke thickness, with big counters in a tall lowercase. Noto Sans Soyombo then keeps a long stretch of text comfortable, thanks to a sizable x-height and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sundanes: A monoline stroke from start to finish makes College unmistakable, with big counters in tall lowercase. And it earns its keep large and short, while Noto Sans Sundanese handles the text with open-mouthed e crossbars.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: College keeps stroke edges parallel through every curve. Noto Sans Sunuwar follows with open, rope-like curves and short ascender stems, so a long passage feels approachable and clear.
gen-dafont-college-gf-noto-sans-syloti-n: College's monoline construction, curves and stems all drawn at one thickness, is its signature, with big counters in a tall lowercase. It does its best work loud; Noto Sans Syloti Nagri quietly reads.
